title: From a log line to a useful error

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A log line says something happened. It rarely says enough to fix it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, you get a message at three in the morning and no idea which release or environment it came from.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That gap is what Serilog dot Sinks dot SentrySDK is for. It's a .NET library by Antoine that connects Serilog logging with Sentry error events, so an error carries its exception, release, environment and request context.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, it's based on an existing community project, serilog-sinks-sentry. And Antoine points out that its GitHub stars measure interest in this repository only, not overall Serilog or Sentry adoption.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A sink receives each Serilog event and hands it to a small wrapper around the official Sentry SDK. That wrapper handles messages, exceptions and transactions, and it also makes the SDK easy to swap out in tests.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Any gotcha for people adopting it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, initialization. The sink sets up Sentry itself, and the README warns against calling Sentry's init a second time in the same process. In a web app that already initializes monitoring, decide who owns it first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What about request data? That sounds sensitive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is. A companion ASP.NET Core package adds request context, but the post says to choose deliberately what leaves your app and to review personal data settings and filtering. There's also a before-send callback for filtering or enriching events.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what do we actually know about quality?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The README documents unit tests, coverage collection and formatting checks. Antoine doesn't claim to have rerun them, and he doesn't invent a coverage number. The package targets net six and net ten.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: dotnet add package, yes. The full post has the architecture diagram and links to the demos.
